name: Fleety
long_description: A typical customer handles 100+ jobs a day, with their best technician generating $500,000 more revenue than the average. Fleety listens to every call and automatically routes each job to the technician most likely to generate the most revenue.
one_liner: Fleety is an AI dispatcher for plumbing and HVAC companies.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Ben and Ariyaman met as students in Montreal. Ben ran a roofing company, then founded Timrep, a contractor permitting startup that reached six-figure revenue and raised from Accomplice. Ariyaman grew an SEO startup to six-figure ARR and automated property management for 3,000+ units.

Before building Fleety, they worked as dispatchers at home service companies. Dispatch decides how much a shop makes, but it runs on gut feel and bad data. Jobs go to whoever is free, not the tech most likely to close.

They moved to San Francisco to fix that, starting with dispatch.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Plenty of startups help plumbing and HVAC shops answer phones and book jobs. But once a job is booked, someone still has to decide who to send, and keep moving things around as the day changes.

We spent months working as dispatchers and found it was one of the hardest parts of running a shop. You're balancing technician skills, drive time, customer needs, and revenue, all under pressure. And the stakes are high: a shop's best technician can bring in $500K more a year than an average one. Sending the right tech to the right job is how shops earn more from the calls they already have.

That's why we started with dispatch. It touches almost every part of the business and gives us the context to improve other workflows too. Customers are already asking us to build more, and that's how we want to grow: stay close to them and let their needs guide what we build next.

launches.title: Fleety: The AI dispatcher for plumbing and HVAC companies
launches.tagline: Sends the right tech to the right job, and rebuilds the schedule all day.
launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Ben and Ari, cofounders of Fleety.

**TL;DR: Fleety is an AI dispatcher for plumbing and HVAC companies. It decides which technician goes to which job and rebuilds the schedule all day as things change.**

<https://youtu.be/k1n0ZgVW6SY>

_Hear from Alex Nelson, Operational Manager of Panther Services Group, on working with Fleety._

**The problem**

Dispatch is harder than sending the closest tech. One tech won't drive into SF, another can't fit in crawl spaces, and only a few can fix tankless water heaters. Then jobs cancel and techs run late.

Getting it wrong is expensive. A shop's best tech can bring in $500K more a year than an average one. Sending the right tech to the right job is how shops earn more from the calls they already get.

**How Fleety works**

Fleety plugs into ServiceTitan. It checks and fills in job details before they reach dispatch, so jobs are tagged correctly from the start. Then it assigns each job to the best tech for it, based on skills, location, availability and close rate. When the day changes, Fleety rebuilds the schedule.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125686&key=user_uploads/1701704/50d0ea86-2a6a-443f-8a7c-87f19e4004a7)

_Fleety assigning jobs directly on the ServiceTitan dispatch board_

**Results**

At Albert Nahman Plumbing, Heating & Cooling:

\- Fleety makes \~92% of job assignments

\- One dispatcher runs 30+ techs

\- The GM and operations manager are off dispatch, saving \~$60K/yr in overhead
